SF-121: the client secret reaches Secrets Manager through CDK's built-in UserPoolClient.userPoolClientSecret, which adds an AwsCustomResource (Custom::DescribeCognitoUserPoolClient) plus the shared AWS679f53fac002430cb0da5b7982bd2287 provider Lambda and an IAM policy allowing cognito-idp:DescribeUserPoolClient on this pool's ARN. CloudFormation keeps the describe response as a custom-resource attribute (readable only through GetAtt); the provider hides it from its logs only while the feature flag @aws-cdk/cognito:logUserPoolClientSecretValue stays off (cdk.json does not set it; T-WINF-2 checks). No esbuild or Docker runs at synth for this task.

SF-121: Cognito's password policy cannot express the 128-character upper bound from Contracts "Password and code rules"; the pool sets only the minimum of 12, so the web server must enforce the maximum (PR 3 domain rules).

SF-122: neither root npm test nor the infra workspace's test script (test/*.test.ts) runs infra/lambda/*.test.mjs, so T-WINF-3 runs only through the brief's explicit `node --test infra/lambda/pre-sign-up.test.mjs`; CI will not run it unless a script or the SF-132 workflow adds it. Changing infra/package.json scripts is outside this task's Files and the package-only allowance, so it was left as is.

SF-122: disposable-email-domains' newest release is 1.0.62 from 2022-09-28 (unmaintained on npm since), so the list is about four years old; it inlines into a 2.6 MB bundle. Per D-118 there is no qa allow-list: qa needs signup-open set to "true" by a person, and a missing parameter means closed.
SF-122: the trigger refuses every sign-up whose callerContext.clientId is not web-client-id, including AdminCreateUser (no client id); nothing in the spec creates users that way.

SF-123: the task's Files list infra/lib/data-stack.ts but not infra/test/data-stack.test.ts, so the CUSTOM_MESSAGE wiring has no committed synth assertion (checked once with a scratch synth); like SF-122's T-WINF-3, T-WINF-5 is not run by root npm test or the infra test script, only by the explicit node --test command.

SF-123: the email is plain text through Cognito's default sender (SES waits for D-77); the same one-sentence message serves sign-up, resent and reset codes, so the email does not say which flow sent it. Admin invites, attribute-change and sign-in code messages keep Cognito's English defaults.

SF-124: T-WINF-6 requires removing the data stack's bucket CORS, which PR 1-era tests T-INF-3 (infra/test/data-stack.test.ts) and T-INF-6 (infra/test/stacks.test.ts) assert, and the new web-client-id read breaks T-INF-6's exact four-name list; neither file is in SF-124's Files. SF-124: with the bucket rule moving to the web stack (D-88) and dev getting no web stack (SF-131), the dev bucket would have no CORS rule at all, so browser uploads from localhost to the dev bucket would fail; SF-127 sets the rule only where a web stack exists.

SF-125: readStageValues gives each stack one reader (fixed construct id StageValues), so later web stack tasks (SF-126 api-url, web-client-id, support-address, bucket-name; SF-128 delete-function-name, which may be missing and would fail the deploy) must add their names to the same call in web-stack.ts rather than call it again. The retention custom resource passes no role: AwsCustomResource's provider is a per-stack singleton, so its policy attaches to the role readStageValues created (StageValuesRole); the test pins that role's grants.

SF-125: the Amplify service role gets only logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on /aws/amplify/<app id>:* as the brief says; AWS's own examples for SSR logging also grant logs:CreateLogGroup and logs:DescribeLogGroups. If compute logs stop arriving on qa, that is the first thing to check (HUMAN qa check, RK-4). Neither Amplify role has confused-deputy trust conditions (aws:SourceArn/SourceAccount): not verifiable offline whether Amplify sets them for the compute role, so the trust is the plain service principal; the reviewer may want a follow-up.

SF-125: bySub is a KEYS_ONLY index (pk and sub only) so no token is copied into it; PR 3's session adapter must Query it for pks and then delete by pk. Sessions table and HMAC secret are Delete on every stage (only the accounts table is retained, D-111); the accounts table has no PITR on qa (the decisions name staging and prod only).

SF-126: infra/lambda/amplify-vars.test.mjs is not in the task's Files but is named by its Verify command, so it was created as the lambda's T-WINF-8 test; like the other infra/lambda tests it runs only through the explicit node --test command, not root npm test or the infra test script.

SF-126: the web stack now reads api-url, bucket-name, support-address and web-client-id at deploy time; a missing parameter fails the deploy. api-url is published by SF-124's ApiStack change, which is blocked (deviation pending), and support-address is set by a person; release.md lists support-address as blocking only the auth tasks' qa check, but it now also blocks the first web stack deploy.

SF-126: the contract table has the web stack write AWS_REGION as a branch variable, and the stack does. Amplify Hosting has been reported to refuse environment variable names starting with AWS_ (reserved prefix); not verifiable offline. If the first qa deploy fails on the variables resource, the likely fix is to drop AWS_REGION from the variables (the compute runtime sets AWS_REGION itself) and change the contract row; the reviewer may want to decide that before the deploy.

SF-126: clearing the roles on delete sends iamServiceRoleArn '' and computeRoleArn '' to UpdateApp/UpdateBranch; the SDK model allows empty strings but whether Amplify treats '' as remove is not verifiable offline (rollback (c) on qa would show it). The app and branch calls run on the Lambda runtime's bundled SDK (installLatestAwsSdk false); computeRoleArn exists in client-amplify since early 2025.

SF-126: the app and branch updates share CDK's AwsCustomResource singleton provider, so its role (StageValuesRole) now also holds amplify:UpdateApp, amplify:UpdateBranch and the conditioned iam:PassRole; T-WINF-8 pins that role's whole grant set. The variables custom resource uses cr.Provider, which adds CDK's framework onEvent function and role (invoke on amplify-vars only). Delete of the variables resource with an empty resulting map would send UpdateBranch with {}; whether Amplify then clears the map is not verifiable offline.

SF-127: SF-124 is still blocked, so the data stack still sets the bucket's CorsConfiguration from webOrigins; once the web stack is wired (SF-131) two writers manage the same bucket rule.
